contract: reward(observation, action, next_observation, info) -> float, the shaped reward used to train a policy on the Gymnasium environment named in the task (info carries the environment's step info such as x_velocity). The evaluator trains a linear Gaussian policy with the cross-entropy method (6 iterations x 16 candidates, 200-step episodes) under the candidate reward and reports the task's own fitness (see README) on 5 evaluation episodes. Higher is better.
notes: Gymnasium Ant-v5; fitness is the fraction of steps with the torso below 0.35 (the paper judged success from videos).

The paper's simulator (Isaac Gym, Bi-DexHands, custom humanoids, ManiSkill2 or a real robot) is replaced by the closest Gymnasium MuJoCo environment and the RL training by a small CEM budget; the fitness definitions are local proxies of the papers' success criteria and scores are comparable within the suite only.
protocol_description: Reimplemented in this repository from the paper's task description; instances are generated locally with a fixed seed, so scores are comparable within the suite but not with the paper's numbers.
name: Ant Lie Down
description: Ant Lie Down: optimize the candidate specified by the paper and evaluate against the named benchmark.
limitations: Upstream commands and dependencies were inspected; costly training, paid APIs, and hardware experiments were not executed.

MuJoCo installation is manual per README. Repository shell script lists handle-pull-v2 but corresponding released reward file is absent; it is not included as a paper task (paper lists ten MetaWorld tasks).

No complete, verified execution adapter has been established for this exact task; this package is an explicit implementation gap.
